subject: Urban Planning
title: Recycling's Dirty Secret
description: A short lesson to help you apply Recycling's Dirty Secret.

hook.text: Only 5% of plastic waste in the US is actually recycled. The rest goes to landfills, incinerators, or overseas dumps.

buildup.text: For decades, the US shipped recyclables to China. In 2018, China's National Sword policy banned contaminated imports.

discovery.text: American cities had no plan B. Recyclables piled up in warehouses, then quietly went to landfills anyway.

twist.text: The plastics industry promoted recycling to avoid regulation. Internal documents show they knew most plastic couldn't be recycled.

climax.text: Aluminum and cardboard recycle well. Plastic mostly doesn't. Reduction and reuse matter more than the recycling bin.

punchline.text: You sorted it carefully. It went to the landfill anyway.

quiz.question: What happened when China stopped accepting US recyclables?
options: American recycling rates doubled as domestic plants expanded
Recyclables piled up and were often sent to landfills instead
European countries absorbed all the excess recycling exports
